findings.reason: the plan must state which of the two names takes the reclaim (the `_at_separatrix` one, whose head matches after the locator is stripped) and which is superseded onto it, or the node cannot execute the stated sequence through the route the section names.
findings.text: the done-when requires "the first of the pair lands on it through the history-apart reclaim the lead ruled for the earlier four names ... and the second is then superseded onto it", and the pair is presented in prose order as `deuterium_tritium_density_flux_surface_averaged_at_plasma_boundary` then `flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_separatrix`; the reclaim named is the `lead_ruled_locator` route the four earlier renames used, whose admission gate — as the section's own cited evidence states it — holds only where "the two ids are one quantity under the two locator vocabularies (`_at_separatrix` and `_at_plasma_boundary` strip to the same head)" (`docs/evidence/fragments/sn-catalog-consistency/scc-separatrix-reclaim.html:13`). The first-listed name's head after stripping the locator is `deuterium_tritium_density_flux_surface_averaged`, while the tombstoned ruled spelling's head is `flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density`: it differs by operator position, not by locator alone, so that route refuses it. Only the second-listed `_at_separatrix` name shares the tombstone's head and can take the reclaim; the first must be superseded onto it instead. As written, a node that reads "first of the pair" as the name listed first is refused at the reclaim and either stalls or reaches for an unsigned path
